Aspire

/uh-SPYRE/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Aspire means to direct one's hopes or ambitions toward achieving something.

Even as a stagehand sweeping between scenes, Nora aspired to direct plays of her own.

Worked Example

The junior park ranger spent her lunch breaks reading wildfire-science journals. She saved for two summers to attend a fire-ecology field course three states away. On her locker she taped a photo of the federal research station in Missoula. When anyone asked why she volunteered for every controlled burn, she said the same thing: one day she would lead a fire-research team of her own. Everything she did pointed toward that single hope — she aspired to it.

Every choice the ranger makes — the reading, the saving, the volunteering — is aimed at one hoped-for future, which is what it means to aspire to something.

How Aspire Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

aim

aim: to direct effort at a goal

strive

strive: to struggle toward

Antonyms

settle

settle: to accept less than hoped

drift

drift: to move without direction

How Strong Is It? — wish → aspire → strive

wish vs. aspire

wish vs. aspire: Wish is weaker — a wish costs nothing and points nowhere in particular; to aspire is to organize your hopes toward one real goal.

strive vs. aspire

strive vs. aspire: Strive is stronger than aspire: aspiring sets the direction of your hopes, while striving is the sweat of actively fighting toward them.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — a-

Prefix — a-: toward (from Latin ad-)

Root — spir

Root — spir: to breathe (Latin spirare)

Put it together

Put it together: Aspire comes from Latin aspirare: ad- (toward) plus spirare (to breathe). To aspire was originally to breathe toward something — to pant after it, straining upward. The breathing root spirare fills English: inspire (breathe into), respiration (breathing), even spirit, the breath of life.

Use the root in a new word: respiration

Use the root in a new word: respiration: The nurse checked the patient's respiration — respiration is breathing itself, from the same Latin spirare that pictures someone who aspires as breathing toward their goal.
